## GitHub Client

Write `megatron/github_client.py`: the ONLY module of the package that talks to the network, stdlib urllib only. It provides API_ROOT, parse_next_link(link_header), urllib_transport(url, headers), class GitHubError(Exception) with .status, and class GitHubClient(token=None, transport=None, sleep=None, clock=None, max_pages=10) with attributes token, transport, rate_limit and `async def fetch_json(self, path)`, exactly as spec section 2.3 describes (headers sent, GITHUB_TOKEN read at construction, the default transport looked up from the module global `urllib_transport` at construction, seconds_to_wait(self.rate_limit, int(clock())) before EVERY request including each page with `await sleep(wait)` when wait > 0, the transport run via loop.run_in_executor, parse_rate_limit after every response replacing self.rate_limit when not None, status >= 400 raises GitHubError, a list body followed along Link rel="next" (case-insensitive header lookup) until no next or max_pages pages, pages concatenated in order; a dict body returned as is). Import parse_rate_limit and seconds_to_wait from megatron.api_manager; do not reimplement them. urllib_transport returns (status, dict(headers), body_bytes) and returns an HTTPError as (e.code, dict(e.headers), e.read()) instead of raising.

Write `tests/test_github_client.py` proving spec section 3 examples A.1-A.8, with a fake transport: a plain function that records (url, headers) of each call and serves (200, headers_dict, body_bytes) from a dict keyed by the full URL; body bytes are the fixture file read in binary. For A.2, page 1 is served at `https://api.github.com/users/torvalds/repos?per_page=5` and pages 2 and 3 at the exact URLs in the `link` headers of pages 1 and 2 (`https://api.github.com/user/1024025/repos?per_page=5&page=2` and `...&page=3`). Expected: 12 items, 3 calls in that order, parse_repo_stats("torvalds", result) gives repo_count 12, non_fork_count 9, total_stars 262425. For A.4 use unittest.mock.patch.dict(os.environ, ...) (clear=True where GITHUB_TOKEN must be absent). For A.5 the fake sleep is `async def` appending its argument to a list; the clock is `lambda: 1790594766`; the served headers are rate_limit_headers.txt with x-ratelimit-remaining set to "0" (reset 1790594886, so the wait is 120). Run coroutines with asyncio.run. Never call urllib_transport.

## Harvest CLI

Write `megatron/cli.py` with `async def harvest(logins, fetch_json, db_path, concurrency=10)` and `def main(argv=None, fetch_json=None) -> int`, and `megatron/__main__.py` that only does `import sys; from megatron.cli import main; sys.exit(main())` under `if __name__ == "__main__":`. harvest awaits collectors.collect_profiles(logins, fetch_json, concurrency), calls processors.score_expertise(pair["profile"], pair["stats"]) for every non-None pair, saves the records with storage.save_experts(db_path, records), and returns {"requested": len(logins), "saved": <records written>, "failed": [logins whose pair is None, input order]}. main parses argv with argparse (prog "megatron", subcommand `harvest`, positional `logins` nargs="+", `--db` default "experts.db", `--concurrency` int default 10). When fetch_json is None, main imports GitHubClient INSIDE the function (`from megatron.github_client import GitHubClient`; that module is written by another card in parallel, so never import it at module level) and uses GitHubClient().fetch_json. main runs harvest with asyncio.run, prints `saved <n> of <m> -> <db>` to stdout and `failed: <login>` to stderr per failure, returns 0 when all saved, 1 otherwise. cli.py imports no network library.

Write `tests/test_cli.py` proving spec section 3 examples B.1-B.4. The fake fetch_json is `async def` serving: `/users/torvalds` -> parsed user_torvalds.json, `/users/torvalds/repos?per_page=100` -> parsed repos_torvalds.json, `/users/minnow` -> a copy of user_torvalds.json with login "minnow" and followers 7, `/users/minnow/repos?per_page=100` -> []; the failing variant raises ValueError for any path containing "minnow". Expected: top_experts(db, 2) logins ["torvalds", "minnow"], expertise_score [850302, 7]. Use a tempfile.TemporaryDirectory for the db. Capture stdout/stderr with contextlib.redirect_stdout/redirect_stderr and io.StringIO. B.4 runs subprocess.run([sys.executable, "-m", "megatron", "harvest", "--help"], cwd=<repo root = parent of the tests directory>, capture_output=True) and expects returncode 0. Always pass fetch_json to main in tests.

## Collect Profiles keeps input order (verification blind spot)

Write ONLY `tests/test_collect_order.py`. Do not write or modify `megatron/collectors.py` -- the author of the criterion is not the author of the code. Why: every v1 test feeds the SAME fixture to every login, so a collect_profiles that permutes its results is invisible; a mutant returning `list(reversed(...))` passes all 40 v1 tests. Your test must make order observable. Prove spec section 3 examples C.1 and C.2. logins = the 5 `login` values of tests/fixtures/search_users_python.json `items`, in file order (karpathy, openai, google, huggingface, rafaballerini). The fake `async def fetch_json(path)`: find the login and its index i in logins; first `await asyncio.sleep(0.01 * (5 - i))` so later logins finish EARLIER; for `/users/<login>` return a deep copy of parsed user_torvalds.json with "login" set to the login and "followers" set to i; for `/users/<login>/repos?per_page=100` return parsed tests/fixtures/repos_torvalds.json. C.1: asyncio.run(collectors.collect_profiles(logins, fetch_json, concurrency=5)) -> [p["profile"]["login"] for p in result] == logins, [p["profile"]["followers"] ...] == [0, 1, 2, 3, 4], [p["stats"]["login"] ...] == logins. C.2: the same with concurrency=2. Import as `from megatron import collectors` and call `collectors.collect_profiles` at call time. The acceptance runs your test against two mutants of collectors.py (completion order via asyncio.as_completed, and reversed) and requires it to FAIL on both.
